region.text: Shengle (Horinger) and the Dai home belt in Inner Mongolia and northern Shanxi

ledger.note: 386: Tuoba Gui restores the state of Dai at Shengle and takes the name Wei. Infobox "Established: 20 February 386"; the text has Tuoba Gui reasserting independence "By 386". The Dai page (opened too): "In 386, taking advantage of Former Qin's rapid decline" he restored the state, first Prince of Dai, then Prince of Wei the same year; Dai had been "conquered in 376 by the Former Qin".

region.text: Later Yan's Shanxi and Hebei

ledger.note: 396: Murong Chui leads a campaign against Wei and the Wei invade Later Yan. "In 396, Murong Chui personally led a campaign against Wei"; the Canhe Slope battle was fought 8 December 395 (Later Yan routed); the invasion of 396 left Later Yan "reduced to Liaoning and parts of northeastern Hebei".

region.text: Zhongshan, in modern Baoding, Hebei

ledger.note: 397: Murong Bao abandons Zhongshan to the Wei. "in 397, Murong Bao was forced to abandon Zhongshan and retreat back to the old Former Yan capital Longcheng"; the Later Yan infobox dates the evacuation 27 April 397.

region.text: the Later Yan shape of 395-401 minus what Later Yan (Longcheng) and Southern Yan (Huatai) kept

ledger.note: 398: the Wei hold most of Later Yan's land. The Canhe page: Northern Wei "by 398 had captured most of the Later Yan's territory". The region is the researcher's reading: Cliopatria's Later Yan 395 shape minus the 402 remnants of Later Yan and Southern Yan.
398: Tuoba Gui moves the capital from Shengle to Pingcheng. "In 398, Tuoba Gui relocated the capital to Pingcheng."

region.text: Later Yan's Shanxi and Hebei

ledger.note: 398: the fighting for Hebei ends with Later Yan reduced to Longcheng and a Southern Yan at Huatai.

region.text: Luoyang, Xuchang, Hulao, Huatai and Sizhou and Yanzhou in western Shandong: the Liu Song lands south of the Yellow River

ledger.note: 422: the Wei invade Liu Song. "After hearing the death of the Song emperor Wu in 422," Mingyuan invaded Liu Song territory. The Liu Song page: "in 422 ... he lost three commanderies to Wei".

region.text: Luoyang and Xuchang (spring 423), Hulao (summer 423), Sizhou and Yanzhou in western Shandong

ledger.note: 423: the Wei take Luoyang, Xuchang and Hulao from Liu Song. Wei captured Luoyang and Xuchang "in spring 423"; "In summer 423, Hulao fell"; Sizhou and Yanzhou (western Shandong) also taken. Not in Cliopatria, whose Wei shape stays at 178 k km2 until 438.

region.text: the steppe frontier north of the Wei lands; the page names no places

ledger.note: 424: the Rouran invade the Wei. "In 424, the Rouran invaded Northern Wei but were repulsed"; "In 429, Northern Wei launched a major offensive against the Rouran and killed a large number of people."

region.text: Xia's Ordos and Guanzhong land

ledger.note: 426: the Wei go to war with Xia. The page dates the war from 426 and the fall of the Xia capital to 427; the Xia page: "After Helian Bobo's death in 425, the Northern Wei intensified their pressure on the Xia."

region.text: Tongwan and the cities of Guanzhong including Chang'an

ledger.note: 427: the Wei storm Tongwancheng and take Guanzhong from Xia. "Wei launched a second attack and captured their capital at the Battle of Tongwancheng" (11 July 427); "Wei carried out a surprise attack on Xia, capturing many cities in Guanzhong including Chang'an". The page does not say which land passed in 427 beyond these cities.

region.text: the Liu Song lands south of the Yellow River

ledger.note: 430: the first Liu Song war ends in the Song recovery of the four cities; the next fighting the page records is 450.

ledger.note: 431: the last Xia emperor falls. "he was ambushed and captured by the Tuyuhun" (431); "Helian Ding's capture marked the end of the Xia"; the Wei page: "In 431, the last Xia emperor, Helian Ding was captured and handed over to Wei by the Tuyuhun". The Xia page has him turned over to Wei in 432. Which land the Wei took is not on the page; Pingliang is the capital of 428-430.

region.text: Xia's Ordos and Guanzhong land

region.text: Liaoxi Commandery

region.text: the steppe frontier

region.text: the Northern Yan realm: Longcheng and Liaoxi

region.text: Northern Yan's Liaoxi and Longcheng

ledger.note: 436: Northern Yan ends.

region.text: Guzang (Wuwei), the Northern Liang capital 412-439, and eastern Hexi

ledger.note: 439: Emperor Taiwu conquers Northern Liang. "the Northern Wei launched a campaign against Northern Liang and placed Guzang under siege ... Mujian surrendered himself to Wei, thus ending the Northern Liang." The Wei page: "Finally, in 439, Emperor Taiwu launched a campaign and conquered the Northern Liang." The Cliopatria Northern Liang 439 shape (93-102 E) lies west of Guzang, so the region is a disc at Wuwei; the western Hexi follows in 441.

region.text: western Hexi: Jiuquan, Dunhuang and the Zhangye-Jiuquan oases

Page silent on who took Jiuquan and Dunhuang: the infobox gives the Northern Liang capitals as Jiuquan 440-441 and Dunhuang 441-442, the Juqu "fled and occupied the oasis city of Gaochang in 442". region.text: the steppe frontier

ledger.note: 443: the Wei attack the Rouran again. "In 443, Northern Wei attacked the Rouran."; then "In 449, the Rouran were defeated in battle by Northern Wei", attacks in 456 and 458.

region.text: the Liu Song provinces south of the Yellow River

ledger.note: 450: Emperor Wen of Liu Song invades the Wei; the Wei counter-invade. "In 450, the emperor attempted to destroy the Northern Wei himself, and launched a massive invasion." "The Wei lured the Liu Song to cross the Yellow River, and then flanked them"; the provinces south of the river were devastated and only Huatai held out.

region.text: the Liu Song provinces south of the Yellow River

ledger.note: 451: the Wei troops withdraw from the south in January. The Wei page: Wei troops withdrew in "January 451".

region.text: the steppe frontier

ledger.note: 458: the last Wei attack on the Rouran that the page dates. "In 456, Northern Wei attacked the Rouran." "In 458, Northern Wei attacked the Rouran." A 492 expedition of 70,000 horsemen follows with no recorded result.

region.text: Xu, Yan, Qing and Ji Provinces: the Liu Song north-east

ledger.note: 466: Liu Song's northern governors defect to Wei after the Liu Zixun rising. "Xue Andu surrendered Xu Province to rival Northern Wei"; Bi Zhongjing of Yan Province joined; the Qing and Ji governors "joined briefly, then returned their allegiance".

Yan Province

ledger.note: 466: Xue Andu surrenders Xu Province to the Wei. The Emperor Ming page: governor Xue Andu "surrendered Xu Province to rival Northern Wei"; the Yan governor Bi Zhongjing joined him. In spring 467 Liu Song generals were routed at Pengcheng and the page ends Emperor Ming's efforts to recapture "Xu and Yan Provinces" in the autumn of 467.

region.text: Xu, Yan, Qing and Ji Provinces

ledger.note: 468: the Liu Song north-east is Wei land.

493: Emperor Xiaowen moves the capital from Pingcheng to Luoyang. Infobox "Movement of capital to Luoyang: 25 October 493"; the text says 494. Xiaowen's sweeping reforms ran through the Taihe period (477-499).

region.text: Hanzhong and Xinyang

ledger.note: 505: Hanzhong and Xinyang fall to the Wei. "by spring 505 Xinyang and Hanzhong had fallen to Wei" after Wei sought to install Xiao Baoyin as a puppet ruler in 503-505. Xiao Yan had founded the Liang in 502 (Cliopatria starts the Liang row in 510).

region.text: the northern frontier garrisons (the Six Garrisons); the page names no sites

ledger.note: 523: the Six Garrisons on the northern frontier rise. Page silent on the start: it dates only the Rouran famine to 523 and the defeat of the "Poliuhan Baling rebellion" to 525; the year is bridged. "Six Garrisons were established to protect the Northern Wei regime from the invasion of Rouran"; conflict between elites and lower-ranking soldiers "helped lead to the dynasty's fall".

region.text: the northern frontier garrisons (the Six Garrisons)

ledger.note: 525: the Poliuhan Baling rebellion is defeated. "The Poliuhan Baling rebellion was defeated in 525." The Rouran page: "Between 525 and 527, Rouran was employed by Northern Wei in the suppression of rebellions"; the Heyin massacre of 528 and Erzhu Rong's rise follow (no land).

region.text: the Western Wei of Yuwen Tai: Guanzhong and Gansu

ledger.note: 534: the western half becomes the Western Wei. The Northern Wei "split into the Eastern Wei and the Western Wei dynasties" in "534-535 AD"; the page names the Western Wei but gives it no date of its own.

region.text: the Northern Wei realm at its end

ledger.note: 534: the Northern Wei dissolves into the Eastern and Western Wei. The Northern Wei page: the dynasty "split into the Eastern Wei and the Western Wei dynasties" in "534-535"; Xiaowu (532-535) is the last emperor.

region.text: the Eastern Wei of Gao Huan: Hebei, Shanxi, Shandong, Henan

ledger.note: 534: Gao Huan installs Yuan Shanjian as ruler of Eastern Wei. "In 534, following the disintegration of the Northern Wei dynasty, he installed Yuan Shanjian as ruler of Eastern Wei"; infobox "Established: 8 November 534". The Northern Wei page dates the split to 534-535, its infobox 8 November 535.

wars.name: Northern Wei-Later Yan war

zones.text: Later Yan land that the Wei held by 398

wars.outcome: Wei victory at Canhe Slope (8 December 395); Zhongshan evacuated 27 April 397; by 398 the Wei held most of Later Yan's land and Later Yan was left at Longcheng.
wars.note: Murong Chui led a campaign in 396 and died that year.

wars.name: Battle of Chaibi
wars.outcome: Later Qin suffered "a heavy defeat to the Northern Wei at the Battle of Chaibi in 402", which halted its eastward expansion; no land change is on the pages.

wars.name: Wei-Rouran wars
wars.outcome: Rouran invasion repulsed (424), Wei offensive (429), marriage alliance (434), Wei attacks 443, 449 (Rouran defeated), 456, 458; a 492 expedition of 70,000 horsemen with an unrecorded result.
wars.note: No page opened places any of these campaigns; the zone is the frontier band.

wars.name: Wei-Liu Song war of 422-430

zones.text: the Liu Song lands south of the Yellow River

wars.outcome: Wei took Luoyang, Xuchang (spring 423), Hulao (summer 423), Sizhou and Yanzhou; in 430 Liu Song recovered Luoyang, Hulao, Huatai and Qiao'ao.

wars.name: Wei conquest of Xia
wars.outcome: Tongwancheng fell 11 July 427, Helian Chang was captured in 428, Helian Ding was captured by the Tuyuhun in 431 and handed to Wei.

wars.name: Wei conquest of Northern Yan
wars.outcome: Periodic attacks from 432; Liaoxi handed over in 433; a major invasion in 436 ended the state and Feng Hong fled to Goguryeo (executed 438).

wars.name: Wei conquest of Northern Liang
wars.outcome: Guzang besieged and Juqu Mujian surrendered in 439; the Juqu remnant held Jiuquan and Dunhuang to 442 and then Gaochang until the Rouran destroyed it in 460.

wars.name: Liu Song-Wei war of 450-451

zones.text: the Liu Song provinces south of the Yellow River

wars.outcome: Emperor Wen's invasion was flanked and destroyed; the Liu Song provinces south of the Yellow River were devastated, only Huatai held out, and the Wei withdrew in January 451. No land changed hands.

wars.name: Wei annexation of the Liu Song north-east

zones.text: Xu, Yan, Qing and Ji Provinces

wars.outcome: Xu and Yan defected 466, Liu Song efforts to recover them failed in 467, Qing and Ji were annexed in spring 468.

wars.name: Wei-Southern Qi war
wars.outcome: "479: Wei prepared to invade Southern Qi, and fighting continued until 481"; a peace treaty was signed with Emperor Wu of Southern Qi in 490. The page gives no land change.

wars.name: Wei-Liang war of 503-505
wars.outcome: By spring 505 Xinyang and Hanzhong had fallen to Wei.
wars.note: Hanzhong's later fate is not on the page.

wars.name: Six Garrisons revolt
wars.outcome: The Poliuhan Baling rebellion was defeated in 525; Rouran forces helped suppress rebels 525-527; Erzhu Rong's massacre at Heyin (17 May 528) and the split of 534 followed.
wars.note: Other rebel groups of the frontier garrisons are not on the pages opened.

certainty.note: Every frontier is approximate: the steppe frontier with the Rouran, the Tuyuhun and Gaochang frontier, the Huai-Yellow River frontier with Liu Song, Southern Qi and Liang. The 490 peace with Southern Qi is a treaty without a described line.

notes: Cliopatria's Northern Wei row 387..533 is a bundle of errors: (1) none of its 14 shapes contains Pingcheng (Datong) or Shengle (Hohhot) in 402-533 although Pingcheng was the capital 398-493 and the Dai home belt stayed Wei land; checked by intersecting each shape with a 30 km disc at Datong and Hohhot (the 387-397 shapes contain both). Corrections add them back as radii. (2) the 451 shape holds Shandong and Xuzhou 15 years before the Emperor Ming page shows Liu Song losing them (Xu and Yan 466, Qing and Ji 468); corrected for 451-465. (3) the 426-438 shape has none of the Xia land (427, 431) or Liaoxi (433, 436), which arrive in the ledger. (4) the Wei begin 386, not 387, and end 534, not 533. The infobox area (2.0 M km2 for 450) is 2.5 times Cliopatria's 790 k km2 for 441-450 and the page gives no breakdown. The 451 shape (1.17 M) is within a factor of two. Page budget: nine new pages (Northern Wei, Canhe Slope, Northern Liang, Xia, Northern Yan, Liu Song dynasty, Emperor Ming, Eastern Wei, Rouran Khaganate); the Later Qin, Later Yan and Dai pages opened for sibling dossiers are cited for single events. Not settled for want of pages: the Wei conquests of the Western Regions (Shanshan, Yanqi, Kucha) in the 440s; the Tuyuhun frontier; the Henan frontier between 430 and 466; the Southern Qi frontier; the Six Garrisons revolt (the Wikipedia article 'Revolt of the Six Garrisons' and 'Six Garrisons Rebellion' would not load) and the later rebel states of 524-534 (a rebel dossier 'six-garrisons-rebels' is suggested, no page opened gives their land). Counterparts without a dossier: dai-sixteen-kingdoms (310-376, 386 predecessor), six-garrisons-rebels. The ledger uses 'liang-dynasty' for the Liang of 502 though Cliopatria starts its row in 510. Disagreements between pages: Eastern Wei 8 November 534 (Eastern Wei page) against 535 (Northern Wei infobox); Luoyang 25 October 493 (infobox) against 494 (text); Daowu's imperial title 24 January 399 (infobox) against the common 398. Gazetteer: all names used resolve (Datong, Hohhot, Baoding, Luoyang, Xuchang, Jining, Zhengzhou, Anyang, Pingliang, Xuzhou, Weifang, Jinan, Hanzhong, Xinyang, Baotou; regions Liaoxi, Henan (region), Shandong (region), Hexi Corridor); the border_band uses the slug rouran-khaganate. Gap: the Cliopatria 451 shape gives Wei 79 % of Henan from 451 (the 441 shape has 6 %); the pages opened date Wei's Henan only in 423 (Luoyang, Xuchang, Hulao, Huatai; lost again 430), after which the 450-451 war ended with a withdrawal, so the Wei acquisition of Henan south of the Yellow River between 431 and 465 is undated and left unexplained in the ledger.
